title: v1/chat adapter: parameter sanitizer, stop/logprobs alignment, and streaming function-call handshake
author: Aisha Singh
description: Motivation: bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions adapter into closer parity with OpenAI semantics for downstream clients while preserving Redwood runtime guarantees. This PR contains three coordinated surface changes: 1) a parameter sanitizer that normalizes OpenAI-style params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop array, presence/frequency penalties, n) into Redwood internal config and rejects ambiguous/unsupported combinations with clear error messages; 2) stop-sequence and logprob handling that ensures streamed deltas and final payloads present logprobs and token boundaries in the shape clients expect, and special-cases legacy clients that rely on trailing stop tokens not being emitted; 3) a streaming handshake for function/tool-calling that removes duplicated function-call tokens between the final streaming delta and the function-call envelope, plus deterministic finish_reasons mapping (stop, length, function_call) across streaming and non-streaming flows. Scope: adapter + streaming runtime framing + tests + docs. Backwards compatibility: the adapter exposes a strict compatibility flag (openai_compat: true) that preserves existing behavior for customers who depend on current Redwood framing. Changes are guarded behind that flag where behavior would otherwise diverge. Testing: unit tests for param normalization, e2e integration tests against the streaming harness, and a Canary job in perf-canary to validate end-to-end latency/regression. High level changes: update the OpenAI compatibility adapter, add a streaming envelope field token_logprobs/partial_delta, normalize role tokens (system->system, user->user, assistant->assistant) including legacy role aliases, and ensure stop sequences are consumed but not duplicated in final outputs. See linked linear tickets for rollout plan and docs updates.
commits: c1a4d8f: add param sanitizer and validator for /v1/chat adapter with error mapping for invalid combos
b2e7f12: implement streaming handshake to dedupe function-call token emission and map finish_reasons consistently
f3d9a01: wire token_logprobs into streaming envelopes and preserve partial delta semantics for clients expecting incremental logprobs
a5b7c3e: tests: add unit and integration tests, update openai-compat.md and SDK adapter shims
review_comments: Jared Kim: Overall design LGTM. Request: please add a short note in docs explaining the compatibility flag and how to opt into strict OpenAI behavior. Also please document the exact shape of the new streaming envelope fields.
Aisha Singh (author): Added docs and a migration_helper that prints recommended client changes. See docs/api/openai-compat.md in this PR.

Maya Ortiz: Found a race in the handshake where a function call could be emitted twice under high concurrency. Suggested moving the dedupe check into the runtime's handshake token buffer and added a unit test that repros the race.
Aisha Singh (author): Pushed handshake.rs update that centralizes the dedupe logic and added the concurrency test. Details in commit b2e7f12.

Owen Li: CI integration failed initially due to a flaky test in tests/stream/integration_function_call.test; suggested adjusting the test harness timeout and isolating network flakiness. After adjustment CI passed.
Jared Kim: Approving after verifying e2e against the Python shim. Left a nit about error wording in param validator which was fixed in a follow-up commit.
ci_checks: benchmarks: warn (streaming_logprob_latency +7% p50 in canary, ticketed ENG-5072)
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions adapter: normalized param handling (temperature/top_p/max_tokens), improved stop sequence and logprob parity for streaming responses, deterministic finish_reason mapping, and reduced duplicate tokens for function/tool-calls in streaming mode. Introduces an openai_compat flag to opt into strict compatibility. Backwards-incompatible behavior is gated behind the flag.
